note: Six adjudicated variants, all of them one word: witness do spells the Hebrew acclamation with j at every occurrence and this edition with i. There is no substantive divergence between the witnesses, and no accidental comparison against tpl, whose profile is substantive-only.

adjudicated.ruling: The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. The i here is consonantal, exactly as in Iesus: the word is Hebrew hallelu-Yah, and the y of the divine name is what both spellings are trying to write. This edition prints i because the books it edits do — the 1962 typical edition sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout — and the apparatus records the j its witness prints.
